name: Napier's logarithms
summary: Napier linked arithmetic and geometric progressions to speed trigonometric calculation; Briggs made decimal tables.

name: Gauge theory transforms four-manifold topology
summary: Solutions of the Yang-Mills and later Seiberg-Witten equations give invariants distinguishing smooth structures on four-manifolds, results unreachable by classical topology.

name: Complex numbers born from the cubic: Cardano and Bombelli
summary: The Cardano-Tartaglia cubic formula gave square roots of negative numbers in the irreducible case, which Bombelli analysed.

name: Fourier integral operators and microlocal analysis
summary: Fourier transforms and symplectic geometry of the cotangent bundle are combined to study singularities of solutions of linear PDE.

name: Sullivan's dictionary: rational maps and Kleinian groups
summary: Iteration of rational maps is matched term by term with the theory of Kleinian groups, so results and techniques of one side suggest and prove statements on the other.

name: Noncommutative algebras, representation theory and number theory
from: algebraic number theory (class field theory, p-adic local theory)
summary: Noether, Brauer and Hasse linked hypercomplex systems to commutative algebra and arithmetic via modules and cohomological ideas.

name: Canonical bases and character sheaves: geometry in representation theory
from: algebraic geometry and topology (intersection cohomology, perverse sheaves)
summary: Intersection cohomology and perverse sheaves give the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials and canonical bases of quantum groups.

name: Deriving the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics
summary: Hilbert's sixth-problem programme of deriving kinetic equations from Newtonian particle systems is carried to long times for hard spheres.

name: Counting complexity (Valiant's #P)
summary: Counting solutions defines a complexity class, and computing the permanent is shown complete for it.

name: Rigorous foundations of algebraic geometry via commutative algebra
summary: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil used valuation and ideal theory to rebuild the Italian school's results rigorously.
